title: WebDAV forced-authentication (DavClnt / WebDAV-MiniRedir) from 10.0.1.4 to 192.168.0.4
summary: On 2020-04-30 between 00:32:18 and 00:32:21 UTC, host 10.0.1.4 (the same address that appears as SCRANTON$ / scranton.dmevals.local in the Windows datasets) issued 36 WebDAV-style HTTP requests to 192.168.0.4:80 — 10 OPTIONS and 26 PROPFIND — with user agents 'DavClnt' and 'Microsoft-WebDAV-MiniRedir/10.0.18362', targeting /webdav and /webdav/. The sequence shows the classic forced-authentication handshake: an initial OPTIONS / with DavClnt returned 403, then OPTIONS /webdav returned 401 Unauthorized, a 301 redirect, OPTIONS /webdav/ returned 401 then 200, and PROPFIND /webdav/ returned 401 then 207 Multi-Status. The 401 challenges followed by successful 200/207 responses indicate the client was induced to present credentials to an attacker-controlled WebDAV endpoint, which is exactly the T1187 credential-capture pattern. This is not normal browsing: the destination 192.168.0.4 is outside the 10.0.0.0/10.0.1.0 corporate ranges used for the DC (10.0.0.4) and peers (10.0.1.6), and the WebDAV-MiniRedir/DavClnt user agents are only produced when Windows resolves a UNC/WebDAV path such as a .library-ms/.searchConnector-ms or shortcut lure. Note the zeek window (2020-04-30) does not overlap the Windows event window (2020-05-02), so this network evidence stands on its own.

However, no forged-ticket artefacts were observed: all 4768 events on the DC newyork.dmevals.local are for pbeesly or SCRANTON$ with PreAuthType 2 and AES256 (0x12), all 4769 requests are for machine accounts (NEWYORK$, NASHUA$, SCRANTON$, WEC$) or krbtgt, and the 4624 logons are the expected machine/system accounts plus pbeesly. No anomalous privileged account authenticated and no 4672 target-user values were returned. The LSASS access is malicious in context, but golden-ticket forging itself is not demonstrated.

title: No silver-ticket evidence: no forged service tickets or anomalous service-account logons
summary: All 4769 service-ticket requests on newyork.dmevals.local in the window are for machine accounts (NEWYORK$, NASHUA$, SCRANTON$, WEC$) and krbtgt, all with AES256 encryption (0x12) and status 0x0, originating from 10.0.1.4 and 10.0.1.6. No service account (e.g. a user SPN account) requested tickets, and no 4672 special-privilege logon target users were returned. The 4634 logoff distribution is 227 type-3 and 9 type-2, consistent with normal network/interactive sessions. The LSASS reads by PowerShell/wsmprovhost are malicious credential access but there is no evidence of forged service tickets being used.

title: No Kerberoasting: no RC4 TGS requests or service-account ticket bursts
summary: Kerberoasting would appear as a burst of 4769 requests for user/service SPNs with RC4 (0x17) encryption. In this window the DC newyork.dmevals.local logged only 4769 requests for machine accounts and krbtgt, all AES256 (0x12), and the zeek kerberos log (2020-04-30, non-overlapping window) shows 14 AS and 11 TGS requests, all for pbeesly/DMEVALS.LOCAL against krbtgt, cifs/NEWYORK, cifs/NASHUA, ldap/NEWYORK.dmevals.local and HTTP/NASHUA with aes256-cts-hmac-sha1-96. No roasting tooling (Rubeus, GetUserSPNs, Invoke-Kerberoast) appeared in process creation or PowerShell script blocks. The LSASS access on SCRANTON/NASHUA is malicious but is not Kerberoasting.

title: No AS-REP roasting: all AS-REQs pre-authenticated, no roasting tooling
summary: AS-REP roasting requires AS-REQs for accounts without Kerberos pre-authentication. Every 4768 in the window (for pbeesly and SCRANTON$) carries PreAuthType 2, i.e. pre-authentication was performed, and the zeek kerberos log shows the expected KDC_ERR_PREAUTH_REQUIRED followed by a successful pre-authenticated AS exchange for pbeesly/DMEVALS.LOCAL. No Rubeus/GetNPUsers/ASREP activity was found in process creation or PowerShell script blocks (the dedicated ES|QL checks returned zero rows).

title: No forged web credential activity; observed credential-access precursor is LSASS access by PowerShell on SCRANTON and by wsmprovhost on NASHUA
summary: No evidence of forged web credentials (no SAML/cookie/token-forgery scripting, no anomalous LogonProcessName, no SSO/ADFS endpoints in Zeek). However, the credential-access precursor is present: on scranton.dmevals.local, C:\windows\system32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\PowerShell.exe (PID 2976, running as SYSTEM) opened lsass.exe with GrantedAccess 0x1f3fff at 2020-05-02T03:05:16.623Z and then 0x1fffff at 03:05:16.654Z, with an UNKNOWN call trace — consistent with LSASS memory access for credential material. On nashua.dmevals.local, wsmprovhost.exe opened lsass.exe with 0x1f3fff at 03:09:29.430Z, but that is explained by the pbeesly PowerShell remoting command 'Get-Process -IncludeUserName' (Invoke-Command -ComputerName NASHUA) seen in 4104 at 23:09:23/23:09:28, i.e. benign. The same user pbeesly also ran Get-PrivateKeys (exporting cert:\LocalMachine certificates to .pfx with password 'saribas') on scranton at 23:04:56, and used PsExec (PSEXESVC.exe) against NASHUA with explicit credentials (4648). Zeek (2020-04-30) does not overlap the Windows window and shows only internal DNS/TLS to 192.168.0.4 with no web-credential endpoints.

title: No MFA request generation observed; hosts show credential theft, lateral movement and archive collection instead
summary: Hunted all four Windows datasets (2020-05-02 02:55Z-03:28Z) for T1621 (Multi-Factor Authentication Request Generation). No MFA/authenticator/OTP/verification-prompt tooling or artifacts were found: a sysmon process-creation sweep for mfa/auth/otp/token/push/login/azure/dsregcmd command lines returned only benign Azure guest-agent and OS components (dsregcmd.exe launched by svchost -k netsvcs -p -s Schedule, TokenBroker/PushToInstall svchost services, CollectGuestLogs.exe, logman.exe, NetworkWatcherAgent.exe); a message-text sweep of windows.other for mfa/multi-factor/authenticator/one-time/verification code/phonefactor returned 0 rows; and the security log shows no failed-logon (4625) or NTLM (4776) burst that would accompany prompt bombing - only a single 4776 for pbeesly from workstation 10.0.1.4. The only interactive logons are two LogonType 10 (User32) events for pbeesly on scranton.dmevals.local from 172.18.39.2. The real attacker activity in this window is credential access and lateral movement, not MFA abuse: on scranton.dmevals.local user pbeesly ran PsExec64.exe from PowerShell four times with the plaintext password of dmevals\pbeesly to launch C:\Windows\Temp\python.exe on NASHUA (03:11:18, 03:12:25, 03:13:28, 03:14:42), each producing a 4648 explicit-credential logon on scranton (source 10.0.1.6) and nashua; on NASHUA the python.exe spawned powershell.exe and cmd.exe, ran a recursive file-collection script (ChildItem over *.doc/*.xls/*.pdf/*.zip/*pst/*psw*/*pass*/*login*/*vpn etc. into $env:APPDATA\working.zip) and staged it with .\Rar.exe a -hpfGzq5yKw to Desktop\working.zip; on scranton pbeesly also ran sdelete64.exe against C:\programdata\victim\???cod.3aka3.scr, Draft.Zip and SysinternalsSuite.zip.
